a hybrid neural network-first principle model is superior to both a pure neural network model and a pure first principle model in terms of its ability to make predictions, its ability to interpolate and extrapolation, and its ability to estimate unmeasured process parameters.
a hybrid network-first principles model is superior to a standard neural network model, and that it can be used for state and parameter estimation and for process optimization.
a hybrid neural network-first principle model can provide a good approximation of a complex process and is more accurate than standard neural network models.

the hybrid network is a powerful and versatile tool for the modeling, estimation and optimization of bioprocesses.
the hybrid network model is a powerful tool for modeling complex processes.

hybrid models are better than standard neural networks and are also easier to implement and interpret.
the hybrid model is a very useful tool for modeling complex processes, particularly when the model is not fully understood.

the hybrid network model is a good alternative to the standard black-box neural network model for modeling bioprocesses, and that the hybrid model is also a good alternative to standard state and parameter estimation methods when a model of the process parameters is available.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a hybrid network-first principles model can be used to estimate the unobserved parameters of a process and hence can be employed to predict the future behavior of the system.

hybrid neural network-first principle modeling can be used to improve the performance of neural network modeling of bioprocesses, especially for the cases where a partial first principles knowledge is available.
a hybrid neural network-first principle model can be a useful tool for modeling and control of bioprocesses.
